cards.design_implication: If measuring the GWB origin, design must include explicit null models (independent pulsar noise and uncorrelated common noise) to quantify the evidence for spatial correlations via Bayes factors or frequentist statistics.
does_not_establish: Causal mechanism of the signal (astrophysical vs cosmological origin).
Generalizability to other PTAs or different time baselines.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The presence of such a gravitational-wave background with a powerlaw–spectrum is favored over a model with only independent pulsar noises with a Bayes factor in excess of $1 0 ^ { 1 4 }$ , and this same model is favored over an uncorrelated common power-law–spectrum model with Bayes factors of 200–1000, depending on spectral modeling choices.
limitations: Applies specifically to the NANOGrav 15-year PTA dataset.
Bayes factor magnitude is sensitive to spectral modeling choices.
cards.statement: In the NANOGrav 15-year data set, the presence of a Hellings–Downs correlated stochastic gravitational-wave background was assessed by comparing the posterior odds and frequentist test statistics against null models of uncorrelated noise.

cards.design_implication: To validate detection significance against false alarms, implement correlation-removal techniques like phase shifting to generate empirical background distributions for the specific null hypothesis.
does_not_establish: The physical origin of the residuals.
That this specific phase-shift method is universally optimal for all PTA analyses.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We have built a statistical background distribution for these latter Bayes factors using a method that removes inter-pulsar correlations from our data set, finding $p = 1 0 ^ { - 3 }$ (approx. 3σ) for the observed Bayes factors in the null no-correlation scenario.
limitations: Calibration depends on the assumption that the null model correctly represents the noise structure.
Specific p-value is tied to the 15-year dataset span.
cards.statement: False-alarm probabilities for detection statistics were calibrated using a phase-shift technique that removes inter-pulsar correlations from the data set.

cards.design_implication: If replicating this study design, restrict the pulsar sample to those with sufficient observation time (e.g., ≥ 3 years) to ensure adequate low-frequency spectral coverage for correlation measurements.
does_not_establish: The optimal baseline length for all future PTAs.
The statistical power of the full set of 68 pulsars mentioned in the dataset description.
cards.evidence_excerpt: For this paper we analyze narrowband times of arrival (TOAs), which are computed separately for sub-bands of each receiver, and focus on the 67 pulsars with a timing baseline <sub>≥</sub> 3 years.
limitations: Sample size is determined by the specific NANOGrav collaboration's data availability.
cards.statement: The analysis focused on 67 pulsars from a 15-year timing data set, requiring a timing baseline of at least 3 years for inclusion.
